stage1_raw_note:
Here is the complete, comprehensive, and faithful clinical SOAP visit note:

**SUBJECTIVE:**

* **Chief Complaint:** Pain at the end of the right middle finger.
* **History of Present Illness (HPI):** The patient, a 41-year-old female, presents with a sharp, stabbing pain at the end of her right middle finger, which began after a car accident a few days ago. The pain is constant, with an intensity of 7-8 out of 10. The patient reports tenderness at the tip of the finger, swelling, and deformity (finger looks a little bent). She is able to move the finger, but with pain.

**OBJECTIVE:**

* **Physical Examination & Vitals:** The patient's vital signs are within normal limits. The physical examination reveals tenderness at the tip of the finger, swelling, and deformity (finger looks a little bent). The patient is able to move the finger, but with pain.
* **Diagnostic Results & Labs:** The X-ray of the right middle finger shows a fracture (distal phalanx).

**ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:**

* **Diagnoses and Clinical Reasoning:** The patient is diagnosed with a distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger. The clinical impression is that the patient has a recent trauma-induced fracture, which is causing the sharp, stabbing pain.
* **Treatment Plan, Medications, and Follow-up:** The patient will be prescribed tramadol for pain management and a finger splint for immobilization. The patient will return for a follow-up X-ray in two weeks to assess the healing of the fracture. The patient will also be advised on pain management strategies and immobilization techniques for the injured finger.

subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Pain at the end of the right middle finger.
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: Hello. I'm a 41-year-old female. I've been having a lot of pain at the end of my right middle finger. It happened after a car accident a few days ago when I got angry and flipped someone the bird, and I hit the ceiling of the car. Doctor: Can you describe the nature of the pain (e.g., sharp, dull, throbbing), its intensity on a scale of 1 to 10, and whether it is constant or intermittent? Patient: The pain is really sharp, like a stabbing feeling, and it's a 7 or 8 out of 10. It's been constant since the accident, doesn't come and go—it just keeps hurting all the time. Doctor: Could you describe any swelling, bruising, or deformity in your right middle finger? Also, are you experiencing any numbness or difficulty moving the finger? Patient: There's some tenderness at the tip of my finger, and it's pretty swollen. I don't think there's any bruising, but it looks a little bent. I can move it, but it hurts a lot when I try. There's no numbness, though. Doctor: Have you experienced any prior trauma or conditions affecting your hand or fingers? Patient: No, I don't think so. I haven't had any previous injuries or conditions affecting my hand or fingers. This is the first time something like this has happened. Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies such as X-rays or MRI for this injury? If so, please provide the results. Patient: I haven't had any imaging studies done yet for this injury. The doctor mentioned looking at an X-ray, but I wasn't told the results yet. I'm just now finding out that there's a fracture in my finger. Doctor: Has the patient been advised on any pain management strategies or immobilization techniques for the injured finger? Patient:
